```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# The consumer demonstration below needs the optional Monocle packages and a
# small fixture data package. It runs only where those are installed; the
# remaining chunks are never evaluated.
have_demo <- all(vapply(
  c("projectData", "monocle3", "BPCells", "projectData.monocle3.testdata"),
  requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE
))
```

# Why a specialised loader?

A Monocle 3 `cell_data_set` (CDS) is an S4 object that bundles an expression
matrix, cell and gene metadata, dimensionality reductions and nearest-neighbour
indexes. For large experiments the counts are usually held as a
[BPCells](https://github.com/bnprks/BPCells) on-disk matrix. Such a CDS cannot
be shipped with `save()` or `saveRDS()`: the R object holds only a *reference*
to a directory that other people do not have. Monocle's own
`save_monocle_objects()` and `load_monocle_objects()` handle this properly by
copying the matrix directory and restoring the object, which means that a data
package needs special handling at both ends.

Two packages divide the work:

| `projectData` (core) | `projectData.monocle3` (this adapter) |
|---|---|
| Registers installed data packages and builds the catalog from metadata | Declares the loader `projectData.monocle3::cds` |
| Resolves object names, attaches collections, handles conflicts | Checks a saved CDS directory is structurally valid (`validate`) |
| Opens a resource lazily, on first access, and caches or retries it | Restores the CDS with Monocle (`open`) |
| Allocates a private working directory for each opening | Puts the restored BPCells files in that directory |
| Knows nothing about Monocle or BPCells | Provides the authoring functions for data package developers |

This vignette covers the Monocle-specific parts only. The general adapter
mechanism (loader contract, manifests, working directories) is described in
`vignette("adapters", package = "projectData")`, and the basic use of
`projectData` in `vignette("projectData", package = "projectData")`.

The loader declaration can be inspected without Monocle installed:

```{r loader}
projectData.monocle3::projectData_loaders()
```

# Creating a data package that ships a CDS

## Prerequisites

Authoring needs `monocle3`, `BPCells` and `SummarizedExperiment` installed.
Because the first two are not on CRAN, install them from GitHub:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
pak::pak(c(
  "blaserlab/projectData",
  "bnprks/BPCells/r",
  "cole-trapnell-lab/monocle3",
  "blaserlab/projectData.monocle3"
))
```

The chunks in this section are not evaluated, because they require a real CDS
and write into a package source tree.

## One call: `save_monocle_cds()`

Work from an existing R package *source* directory (one that has a
`DESCRIPTION`). Assuming `cds` is a `cell_data_set`:

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
projectData.monocle3::save_monocle_cds(
  cds,
  name = "cds_main_adults",
  package_dir = ".",
  overwrite = FALSE
)
```

The `name` must be a syntactically valid R name. It becomes the saved directory,
the placeholder, the manifest resource and the object users will access. The
call creates three things:

```
data/cds_main_adults.rda                 placeholder
inst/extdata/cds_main_adults/            native Monocle serialization
inst/projectData/manifest.dcf            manifest entry
```

* **Packaged backing files.** `inst/extdata/cds_main_adults/` is written by
  `monocle3::save_monocle_objects()` without a tar archive, so the BPCells
  matrix directory and the Monocle index files are installed as ordinary files.
  Counts that are already a BPCells `MatrixDir` are saved as they are.
  In-memory counts (`dgCMatrix`, `dgTMatrix`) are converted automatically, on a
  copy, so your `cds` is not modified. Dense matrices, `DelayedMatrix` and
  HDF5-backed counts are rejected before anything is written.
* **Placeholder.** `data/cds_main_adults.rda` is a small, classed character
  vector. It exists so that `data()`, `R CMD check` and roxygen2 treat the
  dataset conventionally. It is not the CDS; printing it explains that and tells
  the reader how to get the real object.
* **Manifest entry.** `inst/projectData/manifest.dcf` tells `projectData` which
  loader to use. A generated entry looks like this (`Source` uses the
  *installed* layout):

```
Resource: cds_main_adults
Loader: projectData.monocle3::cds
Source: extdata/cds_main_adults
Objects: cds_main_adults
AdapterPackage: projectData.monocle3
RecordedClass: cell_data_set
HelpTopic: cds_main_adults
```

The manifest takes precedence over the placeholder for the same name, so
`projectData` resolves the resource through the loader. The function returns
invisibly a list describing what was written (`directory`, `placeholder`,
`manifest`, `manifest_status`, `replaced`, `removed_stale`).

Saving is staged in a hidden directory inside the package root
(`.projectData.monocle3-stage-*`), validated with the loader's own checks and
only then moved into place; on failure the previous files are restored. An
existing dataset is replaced only with `overwrite = TRUE`, and only if the
existing files are a Monocle save and a recognised placeholder.

## Finishing the package

`save_monocle_cds()` never edits `R/data.R`. Document the dataset as you would
any other, then document, install and declare the adapter as a dependency:

```{r document, eval = FALSE}
#' Adult bone marrow CDS
#'
#' @format A Monocle 3 `cell_data_set` with BPCells-backed counts.
#' @details Access with `projectData::data_attach()`; see the package vignette.
"cds_main_adults"
```

```{r install-pkg, eval = FALSE}
devtools::document()
devtools::install()
```

Add `projectData.monocle3` to the data package's `Suggests` (and to `Remotes`
if it is not on a configured repository). Monocle and BPCells are needed by
*users* only when the CDS is opened.

## Registering directories saved by other means

If you saved a directory yourself with
`save_monocle_objects(cds, "inst/extdata/x", archive_control = list(archive_type = "none"))`
and created a matching placeholder in `data/`, register it with
`write_monocle_manifest()`:

```{r manifest, eval = FALSE}
projectData.monocle3::write_monocle_manifest(package_dir = ".")
```

The function reconciles the manifest with the directories and placeholders
present: it adds or updates entries owned by this adapter, removes entries
whose directory or placeholder has been deleted, and leaves entries of other
adapters untouched. It never deletes saved directories or placeholders, and it
prints a summary only when the manifest changes. `save_monocle_cds()` runs the
same reconciliation. The lower-level details are in `?write_monocle_manifest`.

# Using the data package

## Registering and inspecting

A user needs `projectData`, plus `monocle3` and `BPCells` to open the object.
There is no `library(projectData.monocle3)`: the manifest names the adapter and
`projectData` loads its namespace (without attaching it) the first time a CDS is
requested.

The examples below use the small fixture package
`projectData.monocle3.testdata`; they are evaluated only if that package and the
Monocle dependencies are installed. Substitute your own data package name.

```{r attach, eval = have_demo}
library(projectData)
data_attach("projectData.monocle3.testdata")
```

Attaching registers the collection and reads metadata only. Nothing is opened:

```{r catalog, eval = have_demo}
as.data.frame(data_catalog())[, c("resource", "state", "storage", "loader_status")]
```

The CDS resources are `unopened`. Their `storage` reads `unknown` and
`loader_status` is `unresolved` until the adapter has been loaded, which happens
on first access; the catalog never loads an adapter itself.

## Accessing the CDS

```{r access, eval = have_demo}
data_config(messages = FALSE)
cds <- cds_bpcells_a
class(cds)
dim(cds)
```

The same object can be retrieved without attaching anything with
`data_get("cds_bpcells_a", package = "projectData.monocle3.testdata")`. After
the first access the resource is `ready` and cached; later accesses return the
same restored object without reading the files again.

```{r state, eval = have_demo}
subset(as.data.frame(data_catalog()), resource == "cds_bpcells_a",
       select = c(resource, state, storage, loader_status))
```

Do not use `data("cds_main_adults")` to obtain the CDS. That loads only the
placeholder into the global environment, where it can *mask* the real object.
If you did, remove it with `rm(cds_main_adults)` and use `data_attach()` as above.

# Lazy restoration and disk-backed behaviour

Restoration happens in two stages, both on first access only.

1. **Validation** inspects the saved directory. It reads `file_index.rds` and
   checks that the paths are contained in the directory and that every listed
   file exists. It does not build the CDS or read matrix values, and it runs
   before every uncached open.
2. **Opening** calls `monocle3::load_monocle_objects()`. This rebuilds the CDS
   (metadata, reductions, models) and *copies* the packaged BPCells directory
   into the working directory, then points the CDS at that copy.

Opening a CDS therefore does not read the expression matrix into memory. The
`counts` assay stays a BPCells `MatrixDir` that streams data from disk when
computation needs it:

```{r matrix, eval = have_demo}
counts <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(cds, "counts")
class(counts)
```

The state `ready` in the catalog means that the loader returned, not that the
data are in memory. "Disk-backed" also does not mean "RAM-free": the cell and
gene metadata, reductions and any other assays are ordinary R objects in
memory, and operations that densify or collect counts (for example
`as(counts, "dgCMatrix")`) will load them.

# Working directory and file lifetime

`projectData` allocates a private working directory for each opening of a
resource that needs one, by default under the session temporary directory. The
adapter passes it to Monocle as the location for the restored BPCells files:

```{r workdir, eval = have_demo}
work <- file.path(tempdir(), "projectData-work")
list.files(work, pattern = "tmp$", recursive = TRUE, include.dirs = TRUE)
```

The restored matrix directories sit below `projectData-work/<collection>/<resource>-<n>/`.

What this means in practice:

* The adapter never calls `setwd()` and never writes to your working directory
  or to the installed package, which is treated as read-only.
* Restored files live for the R session. Monocle removes them at exit with its
  own hook; there is no persistent cache in this version, so every new session
  copies the matrix again on first access.
* The counts and the derived row-ordered copy belong to the working directory, so
  the restored CDS does not depend on the installed package for them. The UMAP
  nearest-neighbour index is the exception: it is memory-mapped from the
  installed file. On Linux this keeps working if the package is removed while the
  object is in use, but that is platform behaviour and not a guarantee. Do not
  reinstall or modify a data package in place while a CDS from it is in use;
  on Windows the file cannot be removed while it is mapped.
* **Detaching does not delete anything.** `data_detach()` forgets the
  collection and its cached objects, but it never removes, moves or closes the
  backing files, so a CDS you kept in a variable continues to work:

```{r detach, eval = have_demo}
invisible(data_detach())
dim(cds)
nrow(data_collections())
```

  Accessing the name through `projectData` after detaching and re-attaching
  opens the resource afresh and creates a new copy in a new working directory.
  The old copy remains until the session ends. Backing files are not deleted
  when objects are removed either, as another retained object may still use
  them.

# Supported contents and limitations

**Assays.** The `counts` assay is the one that is stored on disk and restored
as a BPCells matrix. Additional *in-memory* assays (for example `logcounts`) and
*in-memory* alternative experiments (`SingleCellExperiment::altExp()`, such as
ADT or CRISPR modalities, at any nesting depth) are stored with the CDS and
survive a save and a load. This was tested with synthetic data; other
`SingleCellExperiment` extensions are not assumed to be supported.

**Independently disk-backed assays are refused.** Monocle stores a BPCells
alternative assay only as a reference to its original directory, which would not
exist for your users. `save_monocle_cds()` therefore stops *before writing
anything*, with an error of class `projectData.monocle3_external_assay` listing
each offender (for example `altExp 'ADT' / assay 'counts'`). Convert those
assays to in-memory matrices or drop them. The adapter never does this itself,
since it could need a lot of memory. `DelayedArray` assays are also refused.

**Other limits.**

* Exactly one CDS per resource, and the resource name is the object name.
* HDF5-backed saves and CDS saved with in-memory counts are rejected by the
  loader, which is declared disk-backed. A directory saved with
  `save_monocle_objects()` must use `archive_type = "none"`.
* `monocle3` and `BPCells` are `Suggests` only. Registering, cataloguing and
  validating a resource work without them; opening a resource, and authoring,
  need them and fail with a message naming the missing package.
* Monocle functions on the restored CDS need `library(monocle3)`; the adapter
  attaches Monocle only for the duration of the restoration and restores the
  search path afterwards.
* Tested on Linux with monocle3 1.4.27 and BPCells 0.3.0. Windows and macOS
  have not yet been verified.

## Common failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause and remedy |
|---|---|
| Error at open naming `monocle3` or `BPCells` | Optional dependency not installed; install it (see Prerequisites), then call `data_retry()` |
| Validation error mentioning in-memory counts, HDF5 or `file_index.rds` | Directory was not saved by `save_monocle_cds()`/`save_monocle_objects()` with BPCells directory counts and no archive; re-save it |
| `projectData.monocle3_external_assay` at save | A non-`counts` assay, or an altExp assay, is disk-backed; make it in-memory or remove it |
| `projectData.monocle3_conflict` at save | Resource or object name already used by another adapter's manifest entry; choose another `name` |
| `projectData.monocle3_manifest_error` | Existing manifest is unreadable or invalid; it is left untouched, so fix it by hand |
| Access returns a character vector that prints instructions | The placeholder from `data()` masks the real object; `rm()` it and use `data_attach()` |
| An opening failed once and keeps failing | Failures are cached by `projectData`; fix the cause, then `data_retry("<collection>")` |

A failed `data_get(package = )` can leave the collection registered but not
attached, so retry with `package =` again. See
`vignette("adapters", package = "projectData")` for the semantics of failed and
retried resources.
